challenges.title: Two Lines
challenges.task: Print FORTRAN on the first line and IV on the second, with two WRITEs.
hints: A second WRITE (6,20) with its own FORMAT.

challenges.title: Comment the Deck
challenges.task: Start the deck with a comment card, then print 1957.

requirements.message: Start with a comment card: C in column 1.

hints: A card with C in column 1 is a comment.

challenges.title: Seconds in a Day
challenges.task: Compute the seconds in a day (24 × 60 × 60) and print the result as an integer.

challenges.title: Fahrenheit to Celsius
challenges.task: Convert 98.6 °F to Celsius with C = (F - 32) × 5 / 9 and print it with one decimal. Watch out for integer division!

requirements.message: Print with one decimal, like F6.1.

challenges.title: Label and Value
challenges.task: Set K = 42 and print it as ANSWER = 42, label and number on one line.

requirements.message: Print the number with an I format.

hints: Text goes into the FORMAT: 10 FORMAT (' ANSWER =', I3).

challenges.title: The Receipt
challenges.task: Print two lines exactly: COFFEE    1.80 and CAKE      2.50. Use one FORMAT with text and F format for both lines.

requirements.message: Print the prices with F and two decimals.

hints: One FORMAT per line: 10 FORMAT (' COFFEE', F8.2).
And 20 FORMAT (' CAKE', F10.2): the widths make the prices line up.

challenges.title: Jump Over
challenges.task: Set N = 1, then jump over a card that would set N = 2, and print N.

requirements.message: Skip the card with GO TO.

challenges.title: Plus or Minus
challenges.task: Set X = -2.5 and use the three-way IF to print NEGATIVE, ZERO or POSITIVE.
hints: Each branch has its WRITE and a GO TO to the end.

challenges.title: Even or Odd
challenges.task: Set N = 14 and print EVEN or ODD, using MOD and logical IFs.

challenges.title: Teenager?
challenges.task: Set IAGE = 15. Print TEENAGER if the age is from 13 to 19, otherwise NOT A TEENAGER.
hints: Otherwise WRITE NOT A TEENAGER and GO TO 30.

challenges.title: Squares
challenges.task: Print the squares of 1 to 5, one per line, with a DO loop.
hints: K = I * I, then WRITE (6,20) K.

challenges.title: Odd Sum
challenges.task: Add up the odd numbers from 1 to 99 with a DO loop and a step, and print the sum.
hints: DO 10 I = 1, 99, 2 with ISUM = ISUM + I.

challenges.title: Number Staircase
challenges.task: Print 1, 12, 123 and 1234 on four lines. Build each number with an inner DO loop inside an outer one.
hints: Build each number in K: start K = 0 for each line.
Inner loop: K = K * 10 + J for J = 1 to I.
Then WRITE (6,30) K with 30 FORMAT (1X, I4).

challenges.title: Array Total
challenges.task: Store 3, 5, 8 and 13 in an integer array and print their sum, using a DO loop.

requirements.message: Add them up with a DO loop.

hints: ISUM = 0, DO 10 I = 1, 4 with ISUM = ISUM + K(I).

challenges.title: Backwards
challenges.task: Fill K(1) to K(5) with 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 using a DO loop, then print them backwards on one line.
hints: Print with an implied DO: (K(6 - I), I = 1, 5).

challenges.title: Read and Multiply
challenges.task: A data card holds two integers in columns 1–5 and 6–10. Read them and print their product.

challenges.title: The Largest Value
challenges.task: Read integers from data cards (columns 1–4) until the -1 card, and print the largest.
hints: MAXV = 0, then 10 READ (5,20) K with 20 FORMAT (I4).
IF (K .LT. 0) GO TO 30, then IF (K .GT. MAXV) MAXV = K, then GO TO 10.

challenges.title: Big Number
challenges.task: Print Avogadro's number, 6.022E23, in E format with 4 digits.

requirements.message: Use an E format with 4 digits, like E12.4.

challenges.title: Number Grid
challenges.task: Print the numbers 1 to 12 in rows of 4, using one WRITE with an implied DO and FORMAT (1X, 4I4).
hints: The format has room for 4 numbers, so FORTRAN starts a new line for the next 4.

challenges.title: Table Totals
challenges.task: Fill a 3 × 3 table with M(I,J) = I × J and print the sum of each row on its own line.

requirements.message: Use a two-index array like DIMENSION M(3,3).

hints: DIMENSION M(3,3), then fill it with two nested loops.
For each row I: ISUM = 0, then add M(I,J) for J = 1 to 3.

challenges.title: Circle Function
challenges.task: Define a statement function for the area of a circle (3.14159 × R²) and print the area for R = 3.0 with two decimals.

requirements.message: Define a one-line statement function, like AREA(R) = …

challenges.title: Powers of Two
challenges.task: Write FUNCTION IPOW2(N) that works out 2 to the power N with a loop (no **). Print IPOW2(10).
hints: Main: WRITE (6,10) IPOW2(10) with 10 FORMAT (1X, I6).
In the function: IPOW2 = 1, then DO 10 I = 1, N with IPOW2 = IPOW2 * 2.

challenges.title: Banner
challenges.task: Write SUBROUTINE STARS that prints ********. Call it, print WELCOME, and call it again.
hints: Main: CALL STARS, WRITE WELCOME, CALL STARS, STOP, END.
SUBROUTINE STARS with WRITE (6,10) and 10 FORMAT (' ********').

challenges.title: Order Two
challenges.task: Write SUBROUTINE ORDER(A, B) that swaps A and B if A is bigger. Call it with A = 9.0 and B = 4.0 and print both.

requirements.message: CALL ORDER from the main program.

hints: IF (A .LE. B) RETURN skips the swap when they're already in order.
Swap with a spare variable: T = A, A = B, B = T.
Main: CALL ORDER(X, Y), then WRITE (6,10) X, Y with 10 FORMAT (1X, 2F5.1).

challenges.title: Days in Months
challenges.task: Keep the days of the first six months (31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30) in a DATA statement and print their total.
hints: Add them with a DO loop.

challenges.title: Shared Gravity
challenges.task: Put G = 9.81 in COMMON. A subroutine FALL(T) prints the fall distance G × T² / 2 with one decimal. Call it for T = 2.0.

requirements.message: Share G with COMMON in both units.

hints: Main: COMMON G, G = 9.81, CALL FALL(2.0).
D = G * T ** 2 / 2.0, printed with F6.1.

challenges.title: Root of 5
challenges.task: Use 6 rounds of Newton's method from X = 1.0 to find the square root of 5. Print it with 4 decimals.
hints: DO 10 I = 1, 6 with X = (X + A / X) / 2.0.

challenges.title: Cube Root
challenges.task: Find the cube root of 100 with Newton's method, X = (2X + A / X²) / 3, starting at X = 1.0, until the change is below 1.0E-6. Print it with 4 decimals.

requirements.message: Stop when ABS of the change is small.

hints: IF (ABS(XNEW - X) .LT. 1.0E-6) GO TO 20, else X = XNEW and GO TO 10.

challenges.title: Flight Time
challenges.task: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s. Compute the time until it lands, T = 2 × V / 9.81, and print it with 2 decimals.

challenges.title: Highest Point
challenges.task: A shell is fired at 60 m/s at 30 degrees. The highest point is (V × SIN(angle))² / (2 × 9.81). Print it with one decimal.

requirements.message: Use SIN for the upward part.

challenges.title: Area of a Cube Curve
challenges.task: Use the trapezoid rule with N = 20 to find the area under X³ from 0 to 2 (exactly 4). Print it with 4 decimals.
challenges.starter: C     AREA OF A CUBE CURVE
hints: DO 10 I = 1, 19 with X = FLOAT(I) * H and SUM = SUM + X ** 3.
Area = SUM * H, printed with F8.4.

challenges.title: The Area Under X²
challenges.task: Use the trapezoid rule with N = 10 strips to compute the area under X**2 from 0 to 1. Print it with four decimals. (The exact answer is 1/3: why is yours a little bigger?)
hints: DO 10 I = 1, 9 with X = FLOAT(I) * H and SUM = SUM + X ** 2, then SUM = SUM * H.

challenges.title: The Truth Table
challenges.task:
Print the truth table of .AND.: for A and B being .TRUE. or .FALSE., print A, B and A .AND. B with L format, in this order:
T T T
T F F
F T F
F F F
challenges.expectedOutput:
T T T
T F F
F T F
F F F
hints: LOGICAL A, B, then four groups: A = .TRUE. and B = .TRUE., WRITE …

challenges.title: The Job Codes
challenges.task: A deck of job cards has the codes 3, 1 and 2 (keep them in an array with DATA). For each code, jump with a computed GO TO and print PRINT for 3, ADD for 1 and SUB for 2.

requirements.message: Jump with a computed GO TO.
Keep the codes in an array with DATA.

hints: DO 50 I = 1, 3, then K = KODE(I) and GO TO (10, 20, 30), K. Each label writes its word and jumps to 50.

challenges.title: One Third, Twice
challenges.task:
Compute 1/3 as a REAL and as DOUBLE PRECISION, and print both with F20.16. See how many digits are right:
0.3333333432674408
0.3333333333333333

requirements.message: Write the double constants with D, like 1.0D0.

challenges.title: A Complex Product
challenges.task:
Multiply 2 + 3i by 4 - i with COMPLEX variables. Print the product (two F7.2 fields) and its length with CABS (F7.2):
11.00 10.00
14.87
hints: WRITE (6,10) P with FORMAT (1X, 2F7.2), then WRITE (6,20) CABS(P).

challenges.title: Initials
challenges.task:
John Backus led the FORTRAN team. Keep the letters J, B and a full stop in INTEGER variables filled by DATA with Hollerith constants, and print his initials with an A format:
J.B.
hints: INTEGER J, B, DOT with DATA J /1HJ/, B /1HB/, DOT /1H./
WRITE (6,10) J, DOT, B, DOT with FORMAT (1X, 4A1)

challenges.title: The Mirror Card
challenges.task:
Read a 12-column data card with 12A1 into an array, and print it backwards with an implied DO loop:
7591 NARTROF
challenges.starter:
C     THE MIRROR CARD
      INTEGER C(12)

requirements.message: Read one character per element with A1.
Go backwards with a step of -1.

hints: INTEGER C(12), READ (5,10) C with 10 FORMAT (12A1)
